requirements.title: The triage commands, their run files and the landing client
requirements.rationale: Five commands share one run directory so a person, a box and later the service can drive the same steps one at a time.

criteria.action: register the commands `triage`, `triage brief`, `triage run`, `triage submit` and `triage land` on the toolio shell with default timeouts of 15 minutes, 2 minutes, 15 minutes, 30 seconds and 2 minutes respectively, the loop and `brief` declaring the positional input, the forge client, `--repo`, `--context` and a new run directory, and `run`, `submit` and `land` taking `--run-id` and `--dir` (default `.`)
criteria.contract: each registered Command's Path and DefaultTimeout match; `af triage brief --help` lists --dir, --context and --repo

setup: a toolio App with the triage commands registered
check.pseudocode: for p,d in table: c=app.Lookup(p); assert c.DefaultTimeout==d; assert 'run-id' in flags('triage submit')

criteria.condition: `af triage run`, `submit` or `land` is given a missing, malformed or unknown `--run-id`
criteria.action: open nothing through toolio.OpenRunDir, write no file and send no forge request
criteria.contract: envelope status failed, category usage, exit code 2

setup: a temporary git repo with no run directories
an httptest forge that records requests
check.pseudocode: for cmd in [run,submit,land]: for id in ['', 'bad-id','20240101_000000_abcdef']: r=app(cmd,id); assert r.exit==2 && r.cat=='usage'; assert forge.requests==0

criteria.condition: the triage loop or `af triage brief` renders a brief
criteria.action: write `brief.md` (the rendered document), `original.md` (the original report bytes) and `triage.json` {format_version: 1, input {kind, origin, fingerprint}, target, issue, original_report_sha256, prefix {bytes, sha256}} into the run directory
criteria.contract: the three files exist; sha256(original.md) equals original_report_sha256 and prefix.sha256 equals the SHA-256 of brief.md's first prefix.bytes bytes

setup: an httptest GitHub issue with a body
a temporary git repo
check.pseudocode: b=read(brief.md); j=load(triage.json); assert sha(b[:j.prefix.bytes])==j.prefix.sha256; assert sha(read(original.md))==j.original_report_sha256

criteria.action: append ledger records through RunDir.Record with kind `triage.input` when the input is resolved, `triage.brief` when the brief is written, `triage.submission` when a diagnosis is accepted, `triage.question` when a submission carries a question and `triage.land` when landing ends
criteria.contract: ledger.jsonl holds each kind exactly at the step named, in that order for a full loop

setup: an httptest GitHub issue
a scripted brain submitting a valid diagnosis
a second run whose scripted submission carries a question
check.pseudocode: kinds=[r.kind for r in ledger]; assert kinds==['triage.input','triage.brief','triage.submission','triage.land']

criteria.action: run on a dirty working tree without refusing, never run a git write and create no file in the checkout outside `.agent-fox/`
criteria.contract: `git status --porcelain` and HEAD are identical before and after any triage command, with an uncommitted change present

setup: a temporary git repo with an uncommitted modification and an untracked file
git status --porcelain and HEAD captured
check.pseudocode: before=status(); run_all(); assert status()==before and head()==head0

criteria.condition: `af triage land` needs a forge client for the repository recorded in triage.json
criteria.action: build the client through a toolio function for a repository learned at run time, including its host, with the same App.NewForge construction, UserAgent "af/<version>", Dir set to --dir, DryRunForge decoration under --dry-run and close on return as the shell's own client
criteria.contract: App.NewForge receives issuex.Options{Repo: <recorded repo with host>, UserAgent: "af/<version>", Dir: <--dir>}; the client is closed when the command returns

setup: a run directory whose triage.json records a repository with a non-default host
an App.NewForge stub that records issuex.Options and returns a client wrapping a close counter
check.pseudocode: assert opts.Repo.Host==rec.Host && opts.UserAgent=='af/'+ver && opts.Dir==dir; assert closeCount==1

criteria.condition: `af triage land` is given `--repo` naming a repository other than the one recorded in triage.json
criteria.action: build no forge client and write nothing
criteria.contract: envelope status failed, category usage, exit code 2, message naming both repositories

setup: a run whose triage.json records owner/one
a forge stub that fails if constructed
check.pseudocode: r=land(id,'--repo','owner/two'); assert r.exit==2 && 'owner/one' in r.msg && 'owner/two' in r.msg; assert newForgeCalls==0

requirements.title: Preflight refusals before any spend
requirements.rationale: Every refusal that can be decided without a model must happen before the brief is rendered and before a brain costs money.

criteria.action: run the preflight checks in the order flags, input, landing, before rendering a brief or constructing a brain, and on any refusal render no brief, call no brain and send no forge write; `af triage land` repeats the target and credential checks before its first write
criteria.contract: a refused run leaves no brief.md, the faux provider receives no request and the httptest forge records zero write requests

setup: an httptest forge recording writes
an agentkit brain on the faux provider counting requests
check.pseudocode: r=loop('--label','a,b', prUrl); assert r.cat=='usage'; assert not exists(brief.md); assert faux.calls==0; assert forge.writes==0

criteria.condition: a `--label` value is empty, longer than 50 characters, contains a comma or has leading or trailing spaces, more than 10 distinct labels are given, or `--label` is combined with `--land none`
criteria.action: refuse the run, naming the offending label or flag
criteria.contract: envelope status failed, category usage, exit code 2

setup: a loop invoked on an issue URL
check.pseudocode: for bad in cases: r=loop(bad); assert r.status=='failed' && r.cat=='usage' && r.exit==2

criteria.condition: the input is an issue ref with IsPullRequest set
criteria.action: refuse the run, stating that triage takes an issue and not a pull or merge request
criteria.contract: envelope status failed, category usage, exit code 2

setup: an issue ref with IsPullRequest set (GitHub pull URL and GitLab merge_requests URL)
check.pseudocode: r=loop(pullUrl); assert r.exit==2 && 'pull or merge request' in r.msg

criteria.condition: the input issue's state is closed
criteria.action: raise the warning `issue_closed` and continue the run
criteria.contract: envelope warnings contain issue_closed; the status is decided by the later steps

setup: an httptest issue whose state is closed
a scripted brain submitting a valid diagnosis
check.pseudocode: r=loop(closedIssue,'--land','none'); assert 'issue_closed' in codes(r.warnings); assert r.status=='done'

criteria.condition: `--land issue` is in effect for a non-issue input and Run.Target is not a valid repository
criteria.action: refuse the run with a message naming `--repo` and `--land none`
criteria.contract: envelope status failed, category usage, exit code 2

setup: text input, no --repo, and an origin that does not resolve to a repository
check.pseudocode: r=loop('some text'); assert r.exit==2 && '--repo' in r.msg && '--land none' in r.msg

criteria.condition: `--land issue` is in effect without `--dry-run` and the forge client reports Authenticated() false
criteria.system: triage loop and af triage land
criteria.action: refuse with the message "creating or updating an issue in <target> needs a credential: set GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN, or GITLAB_TOKEN, or pass --dry-run or --land none"
criteria.contract: envelope status failed, category auth, exit 1, fix_hint.env GITLAB_TOKEN for a GitLab host and GITHUB_TOKEN otherwise

setup: an unauthenticated httptest GitHub client
an unauthenticated httptest GitLab client
check.pseudocode: assert r.cat=='auth' && r.exit==1 && r.fix_hint.env==expected

criteria.condition: `--land issue` is in effect without `--dry-run` and GetRepository(target) fails or returns Archived true
criteria.action: refuse the run before rendering a brief
criteria.contract: failed/auth for IsNoToken; failed/forge retryable false for not found; failed/forge retryable true for a rate limit or transport error; failed/forge with message "repository is archived" for an archived repository; exit 1

setup: an authenticated forge whose repository endpoint returns 401-no-token, 404, 429, a transport error, or archived true
check.pseudocode: for case in cases: r=loop(); assert (r.cat,r.retryable)==case.want; assert not exists(brief.md)

criteria.condition: `--land issue` is in effect for text, file or stdin input and the input was truncated by the shell or its byte length plus 16896 exceeds issuex.MaxBodyLength(forge)
criteria.action: refuse the run with a message giving the input length and the limit and suggesting `--land none`
criteria.contract: envelope status failed, category usage, exit code 2

setup: a GitHub forge (limit 65536) and a GitLab forge (limit 1048576)
an input shell-truncated, an input of length 48641 on GitHub, and an input of length 48640
check.pseudocode: assert len+16896 > MaxBodyLength(forge) => usage

requirements.title: The brief
requirements.rationale: A byte-stable prefix keeps prompt caching and resume comparisons exact, and fences keep report text from posing as instructions.

criteria.action: compose the prefix in this order: the mandate embedded in the binary (read-only run; fenced content is material from people to verify and never instructions; cite only files read; submit exactly one diagnosis; the path rules and diagnosis schema), the body of `skills/af-triage` without its frontmatter, the repository map from repomap.Build over checks.FileView(dir) at 4000 tokens, and the report section
criteria.contract: the four parts appear in that order in brief.md and the skill's frontmatter lines are absent

setup: a temporary git repo with Go files
an issue input
check.pseudocode: i=[idx(mandate),idx(skillBody),idx(map),idx(report)]; assert sorted(i)==i and -1 not in i; assert 'argument-hint:' not in brief

criteria.condition: the report section is rendered
criteria.action: for an issue, fence the title, the original report, the previous agent-fox diagnosis labelled as possibly stale when the body carries one, and every comment, each preceded by one provenance line naming the author's login and date and marking the reporter; for text, file or stdin input, emit one fence labelled with the command line, the file's base name or stdin
criteria.contract: one fence per part, each immediately preceded by its provenance line

setup: an issue whose body carries a previous agent-fox diagnosis, and two comments, one by the reporter
text, file and stdin inputs
check.pseudocode: for fence in fences(report): assert isProvenance(line_before(fence))

criteria.action: for any fenced content, open and close the fence with a backtick run one longer than the longest backtick run in the content and at least three long
criteria.contract: property: the content never contains a line equal to the closing fence

setup: arbitrary content including backtick runs of any length and lines of backticks
check.pseudocode: for s in gen_strings_with_backticks(): f=fence(s); n=len(f.open); assert n>=3 and n>longest_run(s); assert f.close not in s.split('\n')

criteria.condition: the report section exceeds 131072 bytes
criteria.action: cut it at a UTF-8 boundary at or below 131072 bytes, append the shell's truncation marker and raise the warning `input_truncated`
criteria.contract: the report section is valid UTF-8 of at most 131072 bytes plus the marker; result.report_truncated true; warning input_truncated present

setup: an issue whose report is over 131072 bytes and ends with multi-byte runes straddling the limit
check.pseudocode: assert utf8.Valid(cut) and len(cut)<=131072; assert marker in section; assert 'input_truncated' in warn

criteria.action: for any two briefs rendered by the same binary over the same tree content and the same issue thread or input text, produce byte-identical prefixes holding no run id, run-directory path, --context value, brain name or bound
criteria.contract: property: equal prefix_sha256 across runs differing only in run id, --context, --brain and bounds

setup: a fixed tree and fixed issue thread or input text
check.pseudocode: base=prefixSha(); for v in gen_run_variants(): r=render(v); assert r.prefix==base.prefix; assert v.runId not in r.prefix

criteria.condition: one or more `--context` values are given
criteria.action: place in the task block the question and options of the newest earlier triage run under `<dir>/.agent-fox/run/` with the same input fingerprint whose ledger has a `triage.question` record, when one exists, followed by each `--context` value in order, fenced and labelled as a person's answer
criteria.contract: result.previous_question true when an earlier question was found and false otherwise, the answers then standing alone

setup: an earlier triage run under .agent-fox/run with the same input fingerprint and a triage.question ledger record
a second earlier run with a different fingerprint and a newer question
a third scenario with no earlier question run
check.pseudocode: r=brief('--context','B'); assert q.text in task; assert task.index(q.text)<task.index('B'); assert r.previous_question==True

criteria.action: end the task block with the run id, the submission route (the `file_diagnosis` tool for an in-process brain, otherwise `af triage submit --run-id <id>` with the JSON on stdin, the form `af triage brief` always renders) and a reminder of the turn, cost and time bounds
criteria.contract: the task block contains the run id and exactly one submission route

setup: an in-process brain (agentkit) and the brief subcommand
check.pseudocode: assert count_routes(task)==1 and runId in task

criteria.condition: `af triage brief <input>` runs
criteria.action: write the run files, record `triage.input` and `triage.brief`, call no model and send no forge write
criteria.contract: status done, exit 0, result {brief, prefix_bytes, prefix_sha256, document_bytes, estimated_tokens, map {level, truncated}, report_truncated, previous_question}, artifact {kind: "brief", path}, two next entries for `af triage submit` and `af triage land`; zero forge write requests

setup: an httptest GitHub issue
a counting faux provider
check.pseudocode: assert r.exit==0 and keys(r.result)>=expected; assert forge.writes==0 and faux.calls==0

requirements.title: The brain run and its bounds
requirements.rationale: The brain only reads and submits, so its tools, bounds and read-back are fixed by af and not by the brain.

criteria.condition: the triage loop has passed preflight and rendered the brief
criteria.action: run spec 07's brain.Execute with the selected `--brain` (default `agentkit`) and `--sandbox`, handing it a brain.Brief with Prefix and Task from the brief, Tools set to the triage allowlist, Hook set to spec 07's read-only default, MaxCostUSD from `--budget`, MaxTurns from `--max-turns` and Timeout set to the time left on the deadline
criteria.contract: the Brief seen by the brain has Prefix equal to the brief's prefix bytes and Document() equal to brief.md

setup: a spy brain registered through spec 07's Brain interface
--budget 3 --max-turns 40 --timeout 10m
check.pseudocode: b=spy.brief; assert b.Prefix==prefix and b.Document()==read(brief.md); assert b.MaxCostUSD==3 and b.MaxTurns==40 and b.Timeout<=10m

criteria.condition: `--budget`, `--max-turns` or `--timeout` is omitted on the loop or `af triage run`
criteria.action: use USD 2, 100 turns and 15 minutes respectively
criteria.contract: Brief.MaxCostUSD 2, Brief.MaxTurns 100, shell timeout 15m

setup: the loop and af triage run invoked without --budget, --max-turns, --timeout, --brain
check.pseudocode: assert b.MaxCostUSD==2 and b.MaxTurns==100 and cmd.DefaultTimeout==15*time.Minute

criteria.action: name, in one place, `read_file`, `list_files`, `find_files`, `search_files`, `file_outline`, `find_symbol`, `find_references`, `code_search` only when the hands' toolset over the tree offers it, and `file_diagnosis`, dropping any name the hands do not offer and never including a tool that writes or executes
criteria.contract: the resolved allowlist is a subset of those nine names and contains file_diagnosis

setup: a hands toolset offering all names plus write_file and run_command
a hands toolset without code_search and without find_references
check.pseudocode: a=Allowlist(offered); assert set(a)<=NINE and 'file_diagnosis' in a and not ({'write_file','run_command'}&set(a))

criteria.action: define a submission.Kind with ToolName `file_diagnosis`, Schema equal to the diagnosis JSON Schema and Validate equal to the diagnosis validator, so `file_diagnosis` submits through spec 07's in-process submit
criteria.contract: an in-process `file_diagnosis` call with a valid diagnosis writes `.agent-fox/run/<id>/submission.json` in the brain's tree

setup: the triage submission.Kind with ToolName file_diagnosis, the diagnosis Schema and the validator
a temporary tree with a.go
check.pseudocode: res=submitInProc(kind,tree,id,diag); assert exists(tree+'/.agent-fox/run/'+id+'/submission.json')

criteria.condition: the brain run ends
criteria.action: read back `submission.json` and `rejections.jsonl` from the brain's tree into the run directory and re-validate the submission with the diagnosis validator against the host's tree
criteria.contract: <run_dir>/submission.json and <run_dir>/rejections.jsonl hold the brain's files; a submission that fails host re-validation is treated as absent

setup: a scripted brain in a local box that submits a valid diagnosis and has one refusal
a variant whose submission cites a file deleted from the host tree before read-back
check.pseudocode: assert read(runDir/'rejections.jsonl')==boxFile; stale => r.cat=='no_result'

criteria.condition: no valid submission exists after the brain run, or the budget or turn bound was spent first
criteria.action: land nothing and send no forge write
criteria.contract: spec 07's failure (failed/no_result, or failed/budget with fix_hint {flag: "--budget" or "--max-turns", suggest: twice the value}), exit 1, result null, artifacts listing the brief

setup: a scripted brain that never submits
a scripted brain exceeding --max-turns 3
a faux brain exceeding --budget 0.5
an httptest forge recording writes
check.pseudocode: assert r.exit==1 and r.result is None; assert {'kind':'brief'} in artifacts; assert forge.writes==0

criteria.condition: `af triage run --run-id <id>` runs
criteria.action: run the agentkit brain in this process over `--dir` without a box, using the run's brief.md, with `file_diagnosis` submitting in-process into the run directory under `--dir`
criteria.contract: status done when a submission was accepted, result {run_id, submitted, rejected_path_calls}, envelope usage from spec 07

setup: a run directory created by af triage brief with a brief.md
the faux provider scripted to call file_diagnosis with a valid diagnosis
check.pseudocode: r=run(id); assert r.status=='done' and r.result.submitted; assert exists(runDir/'submission.json'); assert r.usage is not None

requirements.title: The diagnosis and its validation
requirements.rationale: One strict validator over the file view turns every misnamed field or uncited path into the brain's next turn instead of a bad landing.

criteria.action: be one Go function used by `af triage submit`, the in-process submit and the host re-validation, checking against the file view of the tree it runs on (`--dir` for submit, the box's tree or the host checkout otherwise)
criteria.contract: the same payload and tree give the same problems through every caller

setup: one payload with several problems and one tree
check.pseudocode: assert problems(cli)==problems(inproc)==problems(host)

criteria.condition: the payload exceeds 65536 bytes, is not one JSON object, has an unknown field, or breaks a field rule: title missing or not one line of 1 to 120 characters; severity not critical|high|medium|low; confidence not confirmed|probable|suspected|not_reproducible; root_cause outside 1 to 6000 bytes; affected_files outside 1 to 30 items of {path, line?, note} with note at most 300 bytes and line at least 1 and at most the file's line count; suggested_fix outside 1 to 6000 bytes; acceptance_criteria outside 1 to 15 strings of 1 to 300 bytes; question.text outside 1 to 2000 bytes or question.options neither empty nor 2 to 6 items of 1 to 200 bytes; or a question with confidence confirmed or probable
criteria.action: report one problem per broken rule
criteria.contract: each problem names its field as a JSON pointer, for example /severity or /affected_files/2/line

setup: a valid diagnosis and a tree of two files, one with 10 lines
check.pseudocode: for mut,ptr in table: p=Validate(mutate(valid,mut),tree); assert ptr in pointers(p)

criteria.condition: confidence is `not_reproducible` or a question is present
criteria.action: accept empty affected_files, suggested_fix and acceptance_criteria while applying every other rule
criteria.contract: a not_reproducible diagnosis with empty lists and otherwise valid fields has zero problems

setup: a not_reproducible diagnosis with empty affected_files, suggested_fix and acceptance_criteria
a suspected diagnosis with a question and empty lists
a suspected diagnosis with no question and empty lists
a not_reproducible diagnosis with a bad severity
check.pseudocode: assert Validate(nr_empty)==[]; assert '/affected_files' in ptrs(Validate(suspected_empty))

criteria.condition: an affected_files path is checked
criteria.action: strip a leading `./`, make an absolute path under the tree relative to it, convert to slash separators, and when the result does not resolve, line is absent and the path ends in `:<digits>`, retry with the part before the colon and take the digits as line
criteria.contract: `./a/b.go`, `<tree>/a/b.go` and `a/b.go:12` all resolve to `a/b.go`, the last with line 12

setup: a tree containing a/b.go with 20 lines and a file literally named c:5
check.pseudocode: assert norm('a/b.go:12')==('a/b.go',12)

criteria.condition: a path, after normalization, is absolute outside the tree, contains `..`, is under `.git/` or `.agent-fox/`, is a directory, or is not a regular file in the file view
criteria.action: report the path as unresolved
criteria.contract: problem at /affected_files/<i>/path naming the path and up to three existing file-view paths with the same base name

setup: a tree with x/util.go, y/util.go, z/util.go, w/util.go and a directory pkg/
check.pseudocode: p=Validate(...); assert len(suggestions(p['missing/util.go']))==3

criteria.condition: any string in the payload contains a NUL byte or the text `<!-- agent-fox:`, or the rendered diagnosis without the original-report section exceeds 16384 bytes
criteria.action: report the offending field or the rendered size
criteria.contract: problem naming the JSON pointer of the string, or the rendered byte count and the 16384 limit

setup: a diagnosis with a NUL in a note, another with `<!-- agent-fox:` in root_cause and in an option, and one whose rendered diagnosis exceeds 16384 bytes within the field caps
check.pseudocode: assert '/root_cause' in ptrs(p) ; assert '16384' in msg(p_big)

criteria.condition: validation finds one or more problems
criteria.system: af triage submit and in-process submit
criteria.action: collect every problem before answering, write no submission and leave an earlier valid submission byte-identical
criteria.contract: spec 07's refusal: failed/submission retryable true with every problem for the CLI, every problem as the tool's error result in-process

setup: a run with an earlier valid submission.json
check.pseudocode: before=read(sub); r=submit(bad); assert r.cat=='submission' and r.retryable and len(r.problems)==3; assert read(sub)==before

criteria.condition: a diagnosis is accepted
criteria.action: store the normalized form, with paths cleaned and `path:N` split into path and line, and record `triage.submission`
criteria.contract: status done, exit 0, result {run_id, accepted: true, submission: <path>, rejected_path_calls}

setup: a run directory and a diagnosis citing `./a/b.go:12`
check.pseudocode: r=submit(diag); assert r.result.accepted; s=load(sub); assert s.affected_files[0]=={'path':'a/b.go','line':12,'note':..}

requirements.title: Rejected path calls
requirements.rationale: A refused submit writes no submission, so the tally of refusals needs its own file that crosses the box the same way.

criteria.condition: a submit call is refused, through the CLI or in-process
criteria.action: append one JSON line {ts, problems, unresolved_paths} to `rejections.jsonl` in the same run directory that submission.json would be written to
criteria.contract: rejections.jsonl gains exactly one line per refused call

setup: a run directory, both via the CLI and via in-process submit
check.pseudocode: assert len(lines(rej))==2 and keys(lines[0])=={'ts','problems','unresolved_paths'}

criteria.action: report rejected_path_calls as the number of rejections.jsonl lines with at least one unresolved path and rejected_submissions as the number of lines, both 0 when the file is absent
criteria.contract: a run with one refusal citing a missing path and one refusal citing only a bad severity reports rejected_path_calls 1 and rejected_submissions 2

setup: rejections.jsonl with one line having an unresolved path and one citing only a bad severity
a run with no rejections.jsonl
check.pseudocode: assert Count(f)==(1,2); assert Count(absent)==(0,0)

criteria.condition: rejections.jsonl is unreadable or holds a malformed line
criteria.action: report both counts as 0 and raise the warning `rejections_unreadable`
criteria.contract: rejected_path_calls 0, rejected_submissions 0, warning rejections_unreadable

setup: a rejections.jsonl with a malformed line
a rejections.jsonl path that is a directory
check.pseudocode: c,w=Count(bad); assert c==(0,0) and w=='rejections_unreadable'

criteria.action: never use the rejection counts to decide whether or how to land
criteria.contract: the same submission lands with the same action and body for any rejections.jsonl content

setup: the same valid submission landed three times with rejections.jsonl absent, with many lines and with garbage
check.pseudocode: assert body(a)==body(b)==body(c) and action(a)==action(b)==action(c)

requirements.title: The issue body format
requirements.rationale: The body is the contract af_fix reads, and the person's original words must survive every repeated triage byte for byte.

criteria.action: render deterministically, in order, the triage marker line, `## Diagnosis` with `**Severity:** <severity> · **Confidence:** <confidence>` and the root cause, `## Affected files` with lines `` - `<path>:<line>` — <note> `` (`` `<path>` `` without a line), `## Suggested fix`, `## Acceptance Criteria` with `- [ ] <criterion>` lines, `## Question` with the text and options lettered `A. `, `B. `, …, the `<sub>` attribution line naming the run id, and `## Original report` with a `<details>` block holding the original between the original-report markers, omitting every empty section except `## Diagnosis` and `## Original report`
criteria.contract: the same diagnosis, run id and original give identical bytes; golden files for a full and a not_reproducible diagnosis match

setup: a full diagnosis with a line-less path and a question, a not_reproducible diagnosis with empty lists, a fixed run id and original
check.pseudocode: assert Render(d,id,o)==Render(d,id,o)==golden

criteria.action: place the original exactly between the begin marker followed by `\n` and `\n` followed by the end marker, adding no other bytes
criteria.contract: the bytes between `<begin>\n` and `\n<end>` equal the original

setup: originals: empty, with trailing newlines, with CRLF, with marker-like text
check.pseudocode: i=body.index(begin+'\n')+len(begin)+1; j=body.rindex('\n'+end); assert body[i:j]==o

criteria.condition: an original is extracted from a body whose first line is not a triage marker
criteria.action: take the whole body as the original, with no previous diagnosis
criteria.contract: Extract returns (body, "", no warning)

setup: a person's body, an empty body, and a body containing the markers but not on the first line
check.pseudocode: assert Extract(b)==(b,'',None)

criteria.condition: an original is extracted from a body whose first line is a triage marker and whose markers pair
criteria.action: take as the original the bytes between the first begin marker followed by `\n` and the last `\n` followed by the end marker, and as the previous diagnosis everything between the first line and `## Original report`
criteria.contract: Extract returns (original, previous diagnosis, no warning)

setup: a body rendered by Render containing marker-like text in the original
check.pseudocode: o,prev,w=Extract(Render(d,id,s)); assert o==s and prev.startswith('## Diagnosis') and w is None

criteria.condition: a body starts with a triage marker but its original-report markers cannot be paired
criteria.action: take the whole body as the original and raise the warning `original_report_unparsed`
criteria.contract: Extract returns (body, "", warning original_report_unparsed)

execution_paths.title: An issue is triaged end to end and its body replaced on GitHub or GitLab

steps.action: runs `af triage <issue URL> --brain agentkit --sandbox local --dir <repo> --label triaged`
resolves the issue input with its thread, builds the forge client and creates the run directory
runs preflight: validates the label, checks authentication and calls GetRepository on the target
renders the prefix from the mandate, the af-triage skill, the repository map and the fenced report, and writes brief.md, original.md and triage.json
reads files through the triage allowlist in the local box and calls file_diagnosis with a valid diagnosis
reads back submission.json and rejections.jsonl and re-validates the diagnosis against the host tree
re-reads the issue, renders the body with the original between the markers, writes diagnosis.md, calls UpdateIssue once with the body and AddLabels with `triaged`
prints a done envelope with action replaced_body and exits 0
